## Status

Draft. Issue #195 remains open. The earlier 189/189 and 192/192 acceptance claims came from suite exits and reversible source envelopes; they did not demonstrate the requested capabilities. The acceptance gate fails when requirement-specific test assertions have not been observed. The [latest CI run](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/actions/runs/36075487835) passes 125/481 cells but still fails 178/189 required capabilities with zero gate errors.

## Changes in this draft

- Translate two narrowly recognized forms into executable target code in both packages: `pub fn answer() -> u32 { 42 }` from Rust to JavaScript, and `console.log(42);` from JavaScript to Rust. Tests execute the generated code and detect a changed result or erased print effect. A Rust identifier reserved in JavaScript remains transport-only. Other forms and directed pairs still carry source in a reversible envelope and report a semantic translation obligation.
- Report surface syntax separately from binding resolution, type elaboration, macro expansion, proof elaboration, and project module resolution. Phantom project files and unrelated dependencies no longer make an import appear resolved.
- Record observed malformed-input CST assertions for all 57 inventoried languages in both JavaScript and Rust (114 verification cells). The JavaScript producer test removes one executed callback and confirms the evaluator fails.
- Require per-assertion execution callbacks with test, fixture digest, runtime, commit, and outcome. The evidence producer no longer copies expected assertions into passing results after a green suite. Tests inject missing callbacks, fixtures and assertions, a no-op command, stale/duplicate/skipped records, and the source-envelope regression.
- Run the Rust package's generated JavaScript in Node. The Windows integration test passes its configured MSVC linker to its nested `rustc` process.
- Preserve JavaScript object property names during binding rename, expand shorthand properties and destructuring bindings, and derive block scopes from CST nodes. Shared JS/Rust fixtures verify exact edits and execute both programs against independently specified object keys and values, including Unicode, nested blocks, and aliased object destructuring. The alias case failed in both packages before the fix and passes in both afterward.
- Reject a binding rename that would capture an unresolved reference within the binding's scope in both packages. The regression first failed in both runtimes; an unrelated sibling scope remains renameable.
- Hoist JavaScript `var` bindings to the nearest function scope in both packages and resolve references before the declaration. Shared cases cover blocks, top-level blocks, nested functions and arrow functions; they failed in both runtimes before the fix and now preserve the observed result after rename.
- Allow a binding rename past a nested binding of the same target name when no references would be captured. Shared cases check both nesting directions and still reject actual capture; both runtimes failed the safe cases before the fix.
- Keep the full issue requirement manifest and [generated ledger](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/blob/issue-195-cc10e17ab860/docs/issue-195-requirement-ledger.md) visible. These report unmet capabilities instead of counting unsupported descriptors or package candidates as delivery.

## Reproduction and verification

Before the translation correction, the Rust function example emitted only `__meta_language_portable_v1`, and the JavaScript print example emitted only a Rust comment and dummy constant. Both are now executable for those exact forms. Before the binding correction, renaming `x` to `y` in `globalThis.y = 10; const x = 1; globalThis.result = x + y;` silently changed the final expression to `y + y`; both runtime packages now reject that capture. Before the `var` correction, renaming the declaration in `function f() { if (true) { var x = 1; } return x; }` left `return x` unchanged. Both runtime packages now resolve and rename that reference. The remaining source forms and full-language and full-matrix requirements are still open.

- `npm test`: 172 passed, including the new function-scoped `var` regression.
- `cargo test --all-features`: 35 integration tests, 491 unit tests, and 4 doc tests passed. The focused Rust capture, nested rename, and `var` scope regressions also passed. Clippy, formatting, parity, file-size, crate-size, test-location, and manifest checks passed locally.
- The commit-bound evidence producer ran native validators, candidate npm/crate installation, and pinned RML checks successfully. In the current merge-candidate run (`dde1ff1`), it reported **114/470** substantive cells with complete observed assertion callbacks.
- The [latest aggregate pre-merge gate](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/actions/runs/36075487835) reported **11/189** requirements passed, **178 failed**, across 481 verification cells, of which 125 passed, with 0 gate errors. The 11 passing requirements are fault-injection checks of the gate itself. The last completed report remains unchanged from the prior run: its other 114 passing cells are malformed CST assertions, while positive grammar, representation, translation, conformance, and package-delivery assertions remain missing. Its [uploaded report](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/actions/runs/36075487835) records the remaining failed requirement-specific assertions. This remains an incomplete draft.

## Remaining required work

Full default grammar CST coverage for every language and alias, complete JavaScript/Rust/Lean/Rocq representation and project semantics, all 12 faithful directed translations, construct-level conformance on real projects, and matching published npm/crates artifacts remain required. npm still reports 0.46.0 while the source and crates.io package are 0.58.2. This PR stays draft until independent observed evidence establishes every issue #195 requirement.
